title: Makefile Basics
focus: Make targets, variables, dependencies, phony targets, build/test/clean patterns
rules: ParseMakefile extracts target names in order
GenerateMakefile creates a complete Go project Makefile

flashcards.back: A named rule that specifies how to build a file or perform an action. Format: target: dependencies\n\tcommand

flashcards.front: What does .PHONY mean in a Makefile?
flashcards.back: Declares targets that don't produce files. Without .PHONY, Make checks if a file with that name exists and skips the rule if it does.

flashcards.front: What is $@ in a Makefile recipe?
flashcards.back: The automatic variable for the target name. $< is the first prerequisite. $? is prerequisites newer than the target.

flashcards.front: What is the difference between = and := in Makefile variables?
flashcards.back: = is recursive (evaluated when used). := is simple (evaluated immediately). Use := for performance and predictable behavior.
